sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: What is Groundwater?
**Groundwater** refers to subsurface water found beneath the earth's surface in soil pore spaces and fractures of rock formations, representing about **30%** of the world's fresh water.
When Did Regulatory Focus Begin?

The institutional framework for **Groundwater** management in India accelerated with the establishment of the **Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)** in **1970** (renamed from Exploratory Tubewells Organisation).
Where is it Found?
Stored in geological formations known as **Aquifers**, categorized into **unconfined** and **confined** aquifers across various sedimentary, alluvial, and hard rock terrains.
Who Manages it in India?
Regulated primarily by the **Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)** under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, along with state-level groundwater departments.
Why is it Important for UPSSSC PET?
Crucial for questions regarding India's and Uttar Pradesh's **water resources**, **irrigation dependency (over 60% tube well irrigation)**, and **water conservation** schemes.
Key Features
Characterized by the **Water Table**, recharge zones, discharge areas, specific yield, and permeability parameters.
Significance for UPSSSC PET
High-scoring static GK area covering **Rainwater Harvesting**, **Amrit Sarovar Mission**, and **groundwater depletion** statistics.
Other Essential Facts
**India** is the **largest user of groundwater in the world**, extracting more than the US and China combined, heavily impacting the **Indo-Gangetic plain**.

items.title: 1. Aquifer Types and Characteristics
items.content:
• **Unconfined Aquifer:** Upper surface is the **water table** and is directly exposed to atmospheric pressure through permeable material.
• **Confined Aquifer:** Sandwiched between two **impermeable layers** (aquitards or aquifuges) under higher pressure.
• **Perched Aquifer:** A localized zone of saturation above the main water table due to an impermeable lens.
• **Mnemonic for Aquifer Types:** **U**ncleg **C**an **P**aint (**U**nconfined, **C**onfined, **P**erched).

items.title: 2. Groundwater Conservation and Harvesting
items.content:
• **Rainwater Harvesting (RWH):** Technique of collection and storage of rainwater into natural reservoirs or sub-surface aquifers.
• **Check Dams:** Small barriers built across the direction of water flow on shallow rivers to trap water.
• **Farm Ponds:** Excavated structures to harvest rainwater for supplemental irrigation during dry spells.
• **Mnemonic for Conservation Methods:** **R**avi **C**an **F**arm (**R**ainwater harvesting, **C**heck dams, **F**arm ponds).

items.title: 3. Regulatory Bodies and Acts
items.content:
• **CGWB:** **Central Ground Water Board**, apex national body for scientific studies, monitoring, and assessment.
• **CGWA:** **Central Ground Water Authority**, constituted under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** for regulation and control.
• **State Groundwater Departments:** Implement local state-level acts and NOC approvals for commercial extraction.
• **Mnemonic for Regulatory Hierarchy:** **C**entral **G**overnment **S**aves **W**ater (**C**GWB, **C**GWA, **S**tate bodies).

items.title: 4. Major Threats: Groundwater Depletion
items.content:
• **Over-extraction:** Excessive pumping for agriculture (paddy and wheat) outpaces natural recharge.
• **Salinity Intrusion:** Over-pumping in coastal areas causes saline sea water to contaminate fresh groundwater.
• **Land Subsidence:** Compaction of aquifer layers when water is removed, leading to sinking land surfaces.
• **Fluoride & Arsenic Contamination:** Geogenic contamination affecting the **Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra plain** (especially West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh).

items.title: 5. Government Schemes for Water Management
items.content:
• **Atal Bhujal Yojana (ABHY):** Central sector scheme with **World Bank** assistance for sustainable groundwater management in **7 states**.
• **Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM):** Aiming to provide safe and adequate drinking water through individual household tap connections.
• **Mission Amrit Sarovar:** Launched in **2022** to develop/rejuvenate **75 water bodies** in each district of India.
• **PMKSY (Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana):** Har Khet ko Pani and Per Drop More Crop initiatives.

sections.title: Comprehensive Data Tables
rows: Indo-Gangetic Plain
Extensive alluvial fill with highly productive unconfined and multi-layered aquifers
Supports the highest density of tube-well irrigation in India and faces severe **Groundwater Depletion**.
Peninsular India (Hard Rock)
Granites, gneisses, and basalts with secondary porosity (fractures and fissures)
Low storage capacity; highly dependent on monsoon rainfall and **Watershed** management.
Coastal Regions (e.g., Gujarat, TN)
Alluvial coastal strips prone to over-extraction
Prone to **Salinity Intrusion** into freshwater aquifers.
North-Western India (Punjab, Haryana)
Alluvial plains with intensive paddy-wheat rotation
Critical category blocks due to over-exploitation exceeding **100% extraction stage**.
Bundelkhand Region (UP/MP)
Hard rock terrain, crystalline rocks, and uneven topography
Acute seasonal water scarcity; focal area for check dams and **Mission Amrit Sarovar**.
Western Rajasthan
Desert terrain with saline deep aquifers and sandstones
Relies heavily on traditional structures like **Kunds**, **Baolis**, and **Tankas**.

items.definition: Remember **P-R-E-S-S**: **P**ermeability of soil, **R**ate of recharge, **E**vaporation rate, **S**easonal rainfall, **S**urface slope.
Remember **F-A-N-I**: **F**luoride (dental/skeletal fluorosis), **A**rsenic (skin lesions/cancer), **N**itrate (blue baby syndrome), **I**ron (metallic taste and staining).

items.term: Trick 3: Atal Bhujal Yojana Target States
items.definition: Remember **7 States** via **GU-MA-RA-HA-MP-UP-KA**: **Gu**jarat, **Ma**harashtra, **Ra**jasthan, **Ha**ryana, **M**adhya **P**radesh, **U**ttar **P**radesh, **K**arnataka.
Remember state-wise terms: **Johads** (Rajasthan/Haryana), **Baolis** (Stepwells across North India), **Zing** (Ladakh), **Kuls** (Himachal Pradesh).

items.term: Trick 5: Stages of Groundwater Extraction Categories
items.definition: Remember percentages: **Safe** (<70%), **Semi-Critical** (70-90%), **Critical** (90-100%), **Over-exploited** (>100%).
Remember **Jal Shakti**: Formed in **2019** by merging Ministry of Water Resources and Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Water Table with Aquifer
items.definition: The **water table** is simply the upper boundary of the saturated zone, whereas an **aquifer** is the entire geological body storing and transmitting water.
**CGWB** is a scientific advisory and monitoring board under the Ministry, while **CGWA** has statutory regulatory powers under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**.
Arsenic in groundwater is primarily **geogenic** (naturally occurring from sediment weathering), not purely industrial effluent.
It is a **Central Sector Scheme** with **50% World Bank funding** and 50% central government contribution, not a 100% central grant.

items.term: Mistake 5: Irrigation Source Ranking in India
items.definition: Students often think canals are #1; however, **Tube wells and groundwater** constitute the largest source of irrigation in India (**over 60%**).
Over-exploited means annual groundwater extraction is **greater than 100%** of total annual recharge, meaning reserves are depleting.
**Groundwater** is water held underground in the soil or in pores and crevices in rock.
The upper level of an **underground surface** in which the soil or rocks are permanently saturated with water.
Subsurface geological formations that yield significant quantities of water to wells and springs (**unconfined** and **confined**).
**India** is the highest consumer of groundwater globally, accounting for nearly **25%** of total global extraction.
**Groundwater via tube wells** is the dominant source of irrigation in India and Uttar Pradesh.
Established in **1970**, headquartered in **Faridabad, Haryana**, functioning under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
Mandatory policy initiative for buildings in various states to combat falling **water tables**.
A **₹6,000 crore** scheme launched in **2019** focusing on community-led groundwater management.
**Fluoride** and **Arsenic** pose severe public health risks in several districts of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
Occurs in coastal aquifers when excessive pumping lowers the water table, drawing seawater into freshwater wells.
Holistic management of rainfall and runoff to improve soil moisture and groundwater recharge.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact founding year of CGWB (1970) and the ministry handling water resources (Ministry of Jal Shakti).

Do not confuse 'Arsenic' contamination with 'Fluoride' contamination regarding geographical location; Arsenic is majorly along the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta and plain, while Fluoride is prevalent in hard-rock and arid zones.
Questions frequently test traditional water harvesting names (Johads, Baolis, Tanka) matched with their respective states.
Watch out for statements claiming canals are India's primary irrigation source; tube-wells and groundwater rank first at over 60%.

keyTakeaways: Groundwater constitutes roughly **30%** of the world's total freshwater reserves.
**India** ranks as the world's highest groundwater-extracting nation.
The **Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)** operates under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
**Tube wells** provide the largest share of irrigation water in India and Uttar Pradesh.
**Atal Bhujal Yojana** is implemented across 7 states with World Bank financial support.
Over-extraction leads to severe issues including **land subsidence**, **salinity intrusion**, and **toxic contamination** (Fluoride/Arsenic).
